text:
alex: Heads up — ran into a reproducible failure when running the JS SDK on Vercel Edge. ESM bundle throws at runtime when auth retries should kick in, so requests immediately 401 instead of retrying. Repro in a tiny Next edge route attached.

maya: :eyes: I can reproduce locally on edge-js runtime. Error is `ReferenceError: crypto is not defined`. Looks like our build pulls `node:crypto` from a transitive dep in the ESM entrypoint.

jin: Hmm — our package.json conditional exports map currently points \".\" -> {\"require\": \"dist/cjs/index.js\", \"import\": \"dist/esm/index.js\"} and we publish `dist/esm` with some node-only shims still present. Edge runtime picks the ESM path and chokes.

alex: Right. The weird part is CJS on serverless (node) works fine because the auth retry uses `node-fetch` fallback which uses `http`. On edge it must use global `fetch` and our retry logic tries to access `res.headers.get` but fails earlier because of crypto usage.

maya: Proposed immediate fix: build an ESM-specific browser-friendly bundle that uses the fetch-based auth shim (no node:crypto, no Buffer). Then change conditional exports to include a \"browser\"/\"edge\" target so edge runtimes get that variant. Example snippet: 

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "edge": "dist/esm/edge-entry.js",
    "import": "dist/esm/node-entry.js",
    "require": "dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

jin: That looks sensible. Two follow-ups: 1) types — consumers expect `types` top-level to point at `dist/index.d.ts`. If we switch entry points, we should also author `exports` subpath for types or ensure `types` still resolves. 2) Our bundler currently inlines a tiny retry utility that expects `setTimeout` semantics; edge's timers are fine but we should avoid depending on `process.nextTick` or `globalThis.Buffer` in edge code.

sam: For types we can add \"types\": \"dist/esm/index.d.ts\" and also add \"exports\"[\".\"][\"types\"] = \"dist/esm/index.d.ts\" so TS resolves the right declarations for both edge and node. We should also audit any `#internal` paths that TS might import.

alex: Agreed. Another minor DX issue — the package currently exposes both `module` and `main` fields which confuses some bundlers. I vote we remove `module` and rely on `exports` map only. That simplifies modern toolchains.

maya: +1 for removing `module`. Also let's add a smoke test that runs the published tarball in a minimal Vercel Edge runtime fixture in CI (canary publish step) to catch this going forward. Could be a small playwright-ish script that runs the edge route with the canary package linked.

deploy-bot: canary build queued — job: canary-edge-smoke/1718501234 

jin: Plan: I'll open a PR that (a) emits an edge-friendly ESM bundle (tree-shaken, no node:crypto), (b) updates `exports` with `edge` target, (c) adds `exports` types entry and `types` top-level, (d) removes `module` field. I'll add a CI job that installs from the tarball and runs the minimal edge fixture.

sam: I'll run the SDK quickstarts and confirm auth/retry behavior on both node and edge once the canary is out. If we see differences we can add a small compatibility shim under `lib/edge-shims.ts` that normalizes fetch/res API.

maya: FYI for release notes: call out \"edge-optimized ESM\" and \"types mapping for edge\" and mention that bundlers should prefer `exports` over `module`.

alex: Thanks — ping me when the PR is up and I'll try to break it with our internal sample app (auth-heavy).

sam: Thanks. If we land this quickly we can avoid another support ticket this week. :crossed_fingers:
